findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime field in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint
findings.body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` paginates `AuditLogEntry` with `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` and `order_by="-datetime"`. Unlike `DateTimePaginator`, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `getattr(item, self.key)`, which is a `datetime.datetime` instance on `AuditLogEntry.datetime`, raising `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` whenever results are present. In addition, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of converting it back to a `datetime` object for the queryset filter.

findings.title: Unconditional dereference of organization_context.member can raise AttributeError
findings.body: On line 71, `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated on every GET request before checking `use_optimized`. `organization_context.member` on `RpcUserOrganizationContext` is optional and can be `None` (for example, when authenticated via an organization API token or non-member integration). When `request.user.is_superuser` is `False` and `organization_context.member` is `None`, this raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'`.

findings.title: Negative slice offsets on Django QuerySet raise ValueError
findings.body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 877-886) and `BasePaginator.get_result` (lines 182-184), negative cursor offsets are passed directly as `start_offset` into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when `enable_advanced_features=True` or `cursor.is_prev=True`. Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly rejects negative slice indices with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`, causing an unhandled 500 error whenever a client supplies a cursor with a negative offset. Furthermore, when `cursor.is_prev` is `False` and `offset < 0`, `start_offset` is clamped to `0` for the slice, but the unclamped negative `offset` is still passed into `build_cursor`, corrupting the next/previous cursor offsets.

findings.title: zpopmin can evict the segment root span when capping segment size
findings.body: When `span_count > 1000`, `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` evicts the spans with the smallest `end_timestamp_precise` scores without excluding the root/segment span (`set_span_id`). If child spans finish after the root span (e.g., async children or clock skew) or share the same `end_timestamp_precise` and sort after the root span's payload, `zpopmin` will evict the root span from `set_key` while `has_root_span_key` remains set to `"1"`, causing the flushed segment to be emitted without its root span.
